data.name: Handover_HowTo
data.value: How to run (on the machine to be checked): 1. Open a command prompt with "Run as administrator" (without administrator rights the collection is incomplete). 2. Run: Riegel.Collector.exe If this drive is write-protected: Riegel.Collector.exe --out \\<server>\<share> 3. Note the export path and the SHA-256 the collector prints. Exit codes: 0 complete, 1 written but incomplete, 3 nothing written. Options: --minimal (start no other program), --gzip, --pseudonymize, --deep. Machines on which no foreign program may run: collect-builtin.cmd (built-in Windows commands only).

data.name: Handover_LeavesBehind
data.value: What it leaves behind: it changes no configuration. It writes only its export (and the checksum file) into the chosen folder. Windows itself records that a program ran: temporary files of secedit and gpresult in a fresh %TEMP%\riegel-<random> folder (deleted afterwards), a CLR usage log under %LocalAppData%\Microsoft\CLR_v4.0\UsageLogs, execution traces such as Prefetch and AmCache, and possibly Security log events (4688, 4798, 4799, privilege use). Tell your SOC before a collection round: the collector reads the password policy, local administrators and user rights.
